scope: Independent CPU-only recomputation of post-hoc BF16 rounding hypotheses. Original files unchanged. No NPU calls or producer imports.

checks.source_assertions: Four BF16-representable finite FP32 input arrays, length2048. A/C raw equality established by original and prior independent DTP audit.
checks.independent_rounding: Split FP32 uint32 into high16/low16; increment high16 iff low16>32768 or low16==32768 and high16 odd; shift high16 left16.
checks.tree_structure: 120 unique ordered binary trees; each contains ranks0,1,2,3 exactly once.
checks.comparisons: All recorded A/B mismatch totals and four512-element mismatch counts recomputed and equal.

torch_crosscheck.construction: All65536 high16 patterns except exponent255 (65280 finite patterns), each low16 in[0,32767,32768,32769,65535]; original uint32 RNE formula compared bit-for-bit with torch CPU float32->bfloat16->float32.

limitations: Post-hoc exact matching does not observe or identify the HCCL reduction algorithm; equivalent commutative orderings are not independent device observations.
Checks apply to captured finite BF16 inputs and this rounding hypothesis; generic NaN canonicalization is not claimed.
The wide result uses FP64 accumulation followed by FP32 and BF16 rounding, as explicitly implemented in the reviewed script.
